title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis of Rat Urethral Tissue Following Simulated Childbirth Injury and Microenergy Acoustic Pulse Therapy
content: Microenergy acoustic pulse (MAP) therapy has been associated with functional and structural improvement after childbirth-related urethral injury, but its multicellular ef-fects remain incompletely defined. We explored treatment- and injury-associated dif-ferences in the urethral microenvironment using single-cell RNA sequencing. Eight female Sprague–Dawley rats were assigned to sham, vaginal balloon dilation plus ovariectomy (VBDO), VBDO plus beta-aminopropionitrile (BAPN), or VBDO plus BAPN and MAP (MAP) groups, with one 24-week-old and one 48-week-old rat per group. Urethral tissues were analyzed for cell composition, differential gene expression, Gene Ontology enrichment, stem/progenitor features, senescence-associated secretory phe-notype activity, and CellChat-inferred intercellular communication. A balanced sin-gle-cell dataset comprising 23,128 cells was used for downstream comparative analyses and resolved 19 annotated cell-type/state categories. Across the injury- and age-associated experimental conditions, epithelial, vascular, stromal, immune, and muscle compart-ments showed distinct transcriptional patterns, whereas MAP-treated samples showed a distinct cellular distribution; a separate histological cohort showed higher urethral muscle content. MAP-treated samples also showed differences in CellChat-inferred signaling activity in selected extracellular-matrix, adhesion, vascular, developmental, and neu-ral/neuromuscular pathways, including LAMININ, FN1, COLLAGEN, ANGPT, VEGF, WNT, NOTCH, RELN, SLIT, NCAM, and NRXN. Exploratory enrichment analysis identified treatment-associated differences in translation, oxidative metabolism, stress adaptation, synaptic-organization processes, progenitor-associated transcriptional states, and senescence-related programs. Overall, the findings are descriptive and hypothe-sis-generating and require validation in independently replicated cohorts.
